task.description: WF-02 Step 3b (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) for run-id WF02-REQ019-20260816: independently validate TEST-DESIGNER's test spec and test code for REQ-019 before TEST-RUNNER may start. Hard gate.
acceptance_criteria: resolveTenantByRealm(idp_realm_id) and resolveRealmByTenant(tenant_id) both work against REQ-015's tenants table, tested with the seeded default tenant (bpm-default)
attempting to bind a second tenant to an already-bound idp_realm_id is rejected (unique index or explicit changeset validation), not silently overwritten

attempting to change an existing tenant's idp_realm_id via the normal update changeset is rejected or the changeset simply omits idp_realm_id from its allowed fields — whichever approach is taken, it's stated explicitly in the moduledoc
a realm-ownership guard function exists that rejects a (tenant_id, external_realm) pair where external_realm is not the realm bound to tenant_id

result.summary: Independently read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-019 entry (lines 687-717, confirmed 4 acceptance criteria verbatim-matching the spec's claimed AC1-AC4), test/specs/REQ-019.md in full, and test/letflow/identity_test.exs in full (559 lines) — not TEST-DESIGNER's handoff summary. Cross-checked the test code against lib/letflow/identity.ex, lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex, priv/repo/migrations/20260816000001_create_tenants.exs, and test/support/data_case.ex to verify claims rather than trust them. All 5 checks (a-e) pass for all 4 acceptance criteria plus the two design-flagged rules (default-tenant pinning, oidc_mode-conditional requirement). Independently ran mix test test/letflow/identity_test.exs -> 29 passed, 0 failed (matches TEST-DESIGNER's claim; grep-counted 29 'test "' occurrences in the file as a second cross-check). Independently ran mix test (full suite) -> 97 passed (4 properties, 93 tests), 0 failed (matches TEST-DESIGNER's claim). No @tag :skip anywhere in the file (grepped). No 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the spec (grepped). No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in the test file (grepped for password/secret/postgres:// /ecto:// /DATABASE_URL patterns — zero matches in identity_test.exs itself; config/test.exs's local docker-compose dev credential is outside the test file and is this project's standard config pattern, not something TEST-DESIGNER introduced). Confirmed the migration's partial unique index name (tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index, priv/repo/migrations/20260816000001_create_tenants.exs lines 38-41) matches Tenant.create_changeset/3's unique_constraint/2 declaration character-for-character, so the collision test (case 5) exercises a real, correctly-named DB constraint rather than one that would silently no-op.

checks.check: a — at least one runnable test per acceptance criterion, no @tag :skip without passing counterpart
checks.evidence: AC1: 5 tests (lines 331-360). AC2: 3 tests (lines 364-394, including the converse/distinct-realm case). AC3: 2 tests (lines 398-438). AC4: 4 tests (lines 442-474, one per branch). Plus 6 tests for default-tenant pinning and oidc_mode-conditional rules (lines 478-547). Grepped the whole file for ':skip' and 'TODO'/'FIXME' — zero matches.

checks.check: b — no 'TODO: implement test' left in the spec
checks.evidence: Grepped test/specs/REQ-019.md for 'TODO: implement test' and '@tag :skip' — zero matches. All 19 numbered test cases have concrete assertions described and cite an actual test name that exists in identity_test.exs.

checks.check: c — test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test-pollution risk under the partial unique index
checks.evidence: unique_realm/1 and unique_slug/1 helpers (lines 43-51) use System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) — every test not specifically exercising the 'bpm-default' pinning rule uses these. The literal "bpm-default" appears only in tests that are deliberately testing the pinning rule itself (lines 65-67, 331-341, 478-511) — confirmed each such test is self-contained (builds its own tenant row inside its own test body, no shared setup/fixture block creating a 'bpm-default' row once for multiple tests to share).

checks.check: d — tests self-sufficient, no execution-order dependency
checks.evidence: Every test builds its own tenant/user rows via insert_tenant!/insert_default_tenant! inside its own test body; none reads state left behind by another test. use Letflow.DataCase, async: true (line 32) is only safe under per-test isolation, which the sandbox mode check below confirms.

checks.check: e — no hardcoded secrets/connection strings in test files
checks.evidence: Grepped identity_test.exs for password/secret/postgres:// /ecto:// /DATABASE_URL/conn_str patterns — zero matches. The only credential-shaped string in the config chain (config/test.exs's password: "letflow") is outside the file under review and is a local docker-compose dev-only credential, this project's existing config pattern.

checks.check: verify_realm_ownership/2's 4 branches are separate test cases, not collapsed
checks.evidence: Read lines 442-474 directly: 4 distinct 'test' blocks — match (line 442), mismatch (line 449), not-found (line 460), nil-bound-realm (line 465) — each with its own fixture and its own single-purpose assertion. None of the 4 assertions could pass under a subtly-broken implementation of a different branch (e.g. the mismatch test uses a genuinely different bound_realm/other_realm pair, not a value that could coincidentally match).

checks.check: collision test (AC2) asserts the specific unique_constraint error, not just 'fails somehow'
checks.evidence: Line 377-378: asserts {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} = result AND %{idp_realm_id: ["has already been taken"]} = errors_on(changeset) — a specific field-and-message assertion, not a bare pattern match on {:error, _}. Confirmed by reading Tenant.create_changeset/3 (tenant.ex line 86) that this message and field come specifically from unique_constraint(:idp_realm_id, name: :tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index), and confirmed that constraint name matches the real migration index (migration lines 38-41) — so this assertion would fail (not silently pass) if the constraint name were ever misspelled against the DB object, since Repo.insert/1 would then raise Ecto.ConstraintError instead of returning the typed changeset error.

checks.check: immutability test (AC3) checks BOTH changeset non-carry AND persisted non-application (DB re-select)
checks.evidence: Two separate tests read directly: lines 398-415 assert Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :idp_realm_id) == nil at the changeset level (plus that display_name's unrelated change IS present and changeset.valid?, proving the changeset isn't just universally rejecting). Lines 417-438 continue with Repo.update/1 then Repo.get(Tenant, tenant.id) — a genuine re-select from Postgres, not the in-memory update result — and assert persisted.idp_realm_id == original_realm. Both halves are real, distinct assertions against real code paths, matching the spec's claim exactly.

checks.check: fixture realm/slug strings genuinely unique per test; Sandbox mode confirmed to give real per-test isolation before accepting shared 'bpm-default' literal as safe
checks.evidence: Read test/support/data_case.ex directly (24 lines): setup block calls Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo) per test (line 16) — this is Ecto's standard mechanism giving each test process its own checked-out connection wrapped in a transaction that is rolled back when the test process exits, which is genuine per-test isolation regardless of async/shared mode (shared mode, used only for non-async tests, affects whether OTHER processes spawned by a test can see that test's own uncommitted data — it does not cause one test's data to leak into another test's separate checkout/rollback cycle). Confirmed this independently rather than assuming it from the spec's or moduledoc's claim. identity_test.exs runs async: true (line 32), meaning each test gets its own independent checkout with no shared mode — the strongest form of isolation, not a weaker one. Every literal 'bpm-default' use is therefore confined to its own test's transaction and rolled back before any other test runs, confirmed safe.
